# Results (auto-generated by scripts/collect_results.py)

Pooled out-of-fold ROC-AUC on the committed folds. ΔAUC CIs: paired bootstrap over 25 km spatial blocks (Florida, Minnesota) or rows (Kentucky); **bold** = CI excludes 0. `*_tuned` = nested spatial CV, 100 Optuna trials (`baselines/tuned.py`). FMs in fp32. Headline settings were fixed in advance (`results/headline_family.md`): Florida no_landcover × ring × spatial5 and temporal, Kentucky loco, Minnesota sat_nolc × ring × spatial5.

## 2. Seed-aware statistics

### Seed-aware headline statistics

Every model refit with seeds 0..S-1 on the committed folds. `pooled_auc_mean ± sd` over seeds; `seed_avg_auc` = AUC of the seed-averaged prediction. ΔAUC CI: bootstrap over spatial blocks (Kentucky: rows) **and** an independent seed draw for model and reference per resample. DeLong: paired test on the seed-averaged pooled OOF predictions; `delong_p_holm` = Holm-corrected over the family {FM × headline setting} for the given reference.

## 9. Decision analysis

### Decision analysis of OOF predictions

Prioritisation and decision curves are re-weighted to a sinkhole prevalence of 0.091 (1:10); reliability, Brier and ECE are on the 1:1 benchmark sample. `found_per_100_inspected@10%` = expected sinkholes among 100 inspected sites when the top 10 % of sites are visited. `nb_beats_inspect_all_from_pt` = smallest threshold probability from which the model's net benefit exceeds inspecting every site (NaN = never within 0.05–0.8; probabilities prior-shifted to the 1:10 prevalence before thresholding). `platt_*` = after cross-fitted Platt scaling. The FGS favourability map is an ordinal class map (no probabilities), shown for ranking only. Tied scores (FGS classes, random-forest vote shares) enter the ranking curves and ECE as the expected value over random orders of the tied sites, so the numbers do not depend on how the sort breaks ties.

## 11. Statewide maps

### Statewide Florida susceptibility maps (1000 m grid, 147084 land cells)

Each model is fit once on the whole headline table (no_landcover × ring: 2,736 reports + 2,736 ring pseudo-absences) and scores every grid cell; for the FMs this is the deployment mode (one fixed context, no training). `auc_*_vs_land` is a sanity check only: map value at the reports (which were in the context) vs 20,000 random land cells. ## 12. Factor analysis

### Factor analysis (Florida no_landcover × ring × spatial5)

Permutation importance = AUC drop on the test fold when the feature is shuffled (2 shuffles × 5 folds, mean). Group importance shuffles all features of a source together (same row permutation). Partial dependence = mean prediction on a test-fold sample with the feature fixed at 11 quantiles.

## 13. Positional accuracy of the reports

### Positional accuracy of the reports vs model AUC (Florida no_landcover × ring)

## 14. Calibration

### Calibration of OOF predictions (FMs in fp32)

ece = 10 equal-mass bins; slope = logistic calibration slope (1 = ideal, < 1 = over-confident); mean_p_minus_rate > 0 = over-prediction; platt_* = after cross-fitted Platt scaling (fitted on the other folds' OOF predictions; only for fold-based protocols). Kentucky screening: share of depressions to inspect.

## 15. Rotation test

### Rotation test (Kentucky loco)

raw = original features; quantile = per-feature quantile→normal (monotone, trees are invariant); rotated = quantile + random orthogonal rotation of all 10 features (3 rotations). A large AUC loss under rotation means the model relies on axis-aligned structure.

## 17. Spatially separated small-data evaluation

### Spatially separated small-data evaluation (results/buffered, `scripts/buffered_smalldata.py`)

Question: are the small-data advantages of the foundation models interpolation artefacts? Florida = committed table, ring negatives, `no_landcover` (49 factors); Minnesota = shared public-layer schema `sat_nolc` (34). Models: xgboost (hand-set), xgboost_tuned (nested spatial CV, inner groups = 25 km blocks of the training rows), random_forest, TabPFN-3.5, TabICLv2, Kumo-Tabular (fp32, full context). The pair of a positive = its nearest ring negative (`pairs_<region>.csv`).


#### 1. Experiment A — county few-shot with a train–test buffer

Counties with ≥ 100 positives; training = k in-county positives + k in-county ring negatives; 3 seeds; the same fitted model is scored once and evaluated on the in-county rows farther than B km from every training row (B = 0 is the committed design) and on the `neighbours` test (other counties within 50 km of a training row). `paired` = the k positives' nearest ring negatives (random in-county fallback where the pair is outside the county or shared); `independent` = positives and negatives drawn independently. Cells with < 20 positives or negatives are skipped. Δ bands are descriptive: pairs share counties and seeds.

#### 2. Experiment B — buffered learning curve on the committed spatial folds

Test = complete outer fold of the committed 25 km block CV; training candidates = rows outside the fold and farther than B km from every test row; matched stratified draws of n rows (5 reps for n ≤ 1000, 3 for 2000, identical rows for every model), `full` = all candidates. Sampling is independent of pairs (pairs are treated in Experiment A).
